humanities_role_explanation: Islamic scholarly texts (Qur'an, Tafseer, Hadith, jurisprudence from Al-Shamela) supply the material for a generic LLM translation pipeline; the paper does not test disciplinary competence in Islamic studies.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Arabic text translated into English text; OCR uses page images via gpt-4o as a preprocessing step, but the evaluation is on text only.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Forward translation of Arabic Islamic texts to English, validated by back-translation to Arabic and embedding cosine similarity. OCR and RAG for Qur'an/Hadith accuracy are auxiliary pipeline steps and are not evaluated.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Single-task application (translation of Al-Shamela library), not a broad multi-task benchmark; no benchmark is introduced.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: gpt-4o-mini (forward translation and back-translation), claude-3-haiku-20240307 (back-translation); subjective comparison also of Llama 3.2 3B, Qwen 2.5 3B, Silma 9B, Jais 13B, Mistral 7B, gpt-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet/Haiku.

quantitative_metrics.note: Cosine similarity of embeddings between original and back-translated Arabic; share of results >= 0.7.

summary: The paper describes an LLM-based pipeline (gpt-4o-mini, parallelised via API, with optional OCR and RAG) that translated more than 250,000 pages of Arabic Islamic literature from Al-Shamela into English. Quality is validated via back-translation to Arabic by OpenAI and Anthropic models and embedding cosine similarity, plus a crowd-sourced human review process.
key_findings: 71% of OpenAI back-translation results and 86% of Anthropic back-translation results had cosine similarity >= 0.7 (deemed acceptable); the two models' similarity scores are correlated. Model selection was subjective, and gpt-4o-mini was chosen for cost, speed and quality.
facets_explanation: There is no reference answer key: quality is assessed reference-free by back-translation similarity against the original Arabic source, and by an optional crowd-sourced human review where corrections need two reviewers. The paper does not describe annotator expertise or any ground-truth translations.
results_explanation: The paper states '71% of the OpenAI model results and 86% of the Anthropic model results had cosine similarity scores >= 0.7'. These are shares of results above a threshold and not a single headline score on a model-ranking metric, so reported_best_score is null. The number of evaluated pages is not given.

humanities_role.quote: We applied LLM-driven translation automation on a diverse corpus of Islamic scholarly works including: the Qur’an, Quranic exegesis (Tafseer), Hadith, and Jurisprudence from the Al-Shamela library.

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: The LLM prompt query specification is key for driving accuracy and quality in LLM’s response to users’ requirements.
